title: Addition with Regrouping
description: Class 3 addition with regrouping (carrying): add 2-digit and 3-digit numbers, understand carrying ones to tens and tens to hundreds, with worked examples and practice.

topics.title: What is Regrouping (Carrying)?
topics.concept:
When we add and a column makes 10 or more, we cannot write two digits in one place. So we regroup (also called carrying): keep the ones digit and carry the extra ten to the next column on the left.

Example: in 27 + 5, the ones are 7 + 5 = 12. Write 2 in the ones place and carry 1 ten to the tens column.

Always add from right to left: ones first, then tens, then hundreds.

Write the ones digit and carry the ten to the next column on the left.
Always add from right to left: ones, then tens, then hundreds.

topics.title: Adding Bigger Numbers & Word Problems
topics.concept:
The same regrouping idea works for 3-digit and 4-digit numbers — you may carry more than once. Stack the numbers so the place values line up, then add each column from the right.

In a word problem, look for words like altogether, in all, total, sum — they tell you to add.

examples.problem: A school has 265 boys and 148 girls. How many children in all?

examples.solution:
• Ones: 6 + 5 = 11 → write 1, carry 1.
  • Tens: 7 + 4 + 1 = 12 → write 2, carry 1.
  • Hundreds: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

So 376 + 245 = 621.

recap: Line up the digits by place value before adding.
You may need to carry more than once for bigger numbers.
Words like 'altogether', 'in all' and 'total' mean add.
